name: useNetwork
summary: Connection type, address and whether traffic actually goes anywhere.
plain: Whether the phone is online, how it is connected, and whether Android marks the active network as metered. Check isConnected before any network call, and isMetered (when it is not null) before a large download.
description: Reads from expo-network: interface type, IP address, reachability and airplane mode. Being connected to Wi-Fi is not the same as having internet, which is why isConnected reflects a usable route rather than merely an attached interface. isMetered comes from the native module: true when the active network lacks NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED (ConnectivityManager), so a metered Wi-Fi hotspot is metered and an unmetered cellular plan is not. It is null when there is no active network or the read is not permitted. isAirplaneMode is null when its read failed.

returns.name: isConnected
returns.desc: Whether a usable internet route exists, not merely an attached interface.

returns.name: isMetered
returns.desc: Whether the active network is metered (lacks NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED). Null before the first read or when Android does not report it. Gate large transfers on it.

returns.name: isAirplaneMode
returns.desc: Whether airplane mode is on. Null before the first read or when the read failed.

returns.name: hasRead
returns.desc: Whether a read has completed. Before it, the values above are defaults.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: `'hardware'` once a read has completed, `'unavailable'` before that.

actions.name: refreshNetwork()
actions.desc: Re-runs the connectivity check immediately, for example when the app returns to the foreground.
actions.output: Resolves once the read completes. Each sub-read fails independently, so one missing value does not blank the rest.

agentNote: Check isConnected before every network call and isMetered before anything large. Never assume Wi-Fi means free or fast.
